Rumors have long suggested that Apple is designing an all-glass new iPhone for next year's 20th anniversary. However, an analyst at Jefferies believes that the device will no longer proceed.

Wall Street analysts say the design plan for a major revamp of the 20th anniversary iPhone has been cancelled

Wall Street firm Jefferies today downgraded Apple stock to "underperform," with analyst Edison Lee pointing out that the possible cancellation of a major design revamp for the 20th anniversary iPhone is one of the main reasons.

The key to this downgrade lies in speculation that Apple's all-glass iPhone project has been cancelled. Although the project was reported as early as 2025 to be under development, with rumors suggesting a launch as early as 2027, Apple has never commented on the speculation. However, the company quietly filed a patent application for a "six-sided glass enclosure" back in 2019. Jefferies had previously considered the launch of an all-glass iPhone to be reasonable and feasible, but Lee believes development work has come to a halt. According to the analyst, supply chain checks indicate that the project was cancelled due to excessively low yield rates. Lee considers this decision "a major setback for driving higher-priced iPhones amid soaring memory costs." If the device launches as scheduled in September 2027 to commemorate the iPhone's 20th anniversary, he estimates the blended retail price will reach US$2,060—higher than the average price of any previous model. Lee wrote: "More importantly, we believe the original plan was to extend the all-glass design to future iPhone Pro and Pro Max models, further boosting their average selling price and profit margins." He believes that amid rising memory prices, this would have been a key defensive strategy.

Lee also pointed out Apple's AI strategy and rising component costs for the iPhone 19 Pro as additional reasons for further downgrading the company's stock rating.

It is unclear from Lee's report whether the analyst is referring to the entire design revamp being shelved, or only certain design elements being cancelled.

Top comment posted by Currentinterest

These analysts have missed the mark many times in their predictions about Apple's future plans. The term "all-glass" may not have even accurately reflected what Apple truly intended to do. The 20th anniversary phone will be uniquely innovative and will sell well regardless of the final design.

For example, there has long been speculation that Apple will not be able to completely remove the Dynamic Island cutout next year. Therefore, an "all-glass" display will not be possible. But the rumored quad-curved design may still be introduced.

In any case, if Apple's iPhone 20th anniversary design has indeed been cancelled, we should receive confirmation from other credible sources soon.

What are your thoughts on this report about the iPhone 20th anniversary design? Feel free to let us know in the comments.
